name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.

notes: FY2026 NII guidance about $105.5bn, or $96.5bn excluding Markets (market dependent)
FY2026 card net charge-off rate guided at about 3.2%
Quarterly dividend raised to $1.65 from 3Q26; LTM net payout 73%
2Q26 reported RoTCE 29% includes a $4.6bn Visa-related gain; 23% excluding significant items
latest.source: JPMorganChase 2Q26 earnings release and presentation (8-K, 14 Jul 2026)

thesis: Scale leader with the most diversified earnings mix among US banks: consumer, wholesale and asset and wealth management.
RoTCE of 23% excluding significant items in 2Q26 is well above any reasonable cost of equity, but part of 2Q26 reflected a pull-forward of deal and markets activity.
The valuation question is sustainability: the market already prices a premium multiple to tangible book.
risks: Credit normalisation in cards beyond the guided ~3.2% net charge-off rate
Lower policy rates compressing net interest income
Markets and investment banking revenue reverting after a strong 2Q26
Capital rules (Basel III endgame, G-SIB surcharge) limiting buybacks
sust_note: Base sustainable RoTCE 19%: between management's 17% through-the-cycle target and the 20.6% five-year average computed from SEC filings (FY2021-FY2025)
